claims.claim: Security fix authored, merged, then generalised into google/go-github, with the credit since recorded in the project's AUTHORS file
claims.detail:
I authored #4556, which was merged by maintainer gmlewis on 2026-09-17: an upload whose URL pointed at a different host than the configured upload host was refused rather than sent with the client's credentials. He reverted it the next day in favour of his broader #4564, which now enforces the general rule in master ('credentials are sent only to configured origins', via AllowedOrigins in github/github.go) and which carries the commit 'Address feedback from sushant-me'.

The Co-authored-by trailer never appeared. On 2026-09-20 the maintainer offered a different mechanism that fits the repository's squash-merge policy: the contributor opens a PR adding themselves to AUTHORS and records the work in its description. I opened google/go-github#4579, and he merged it the same day (2026-09-20T17:11:32Z, merge commit 5493527). 'Sushant Poudel <sushant.poudel2028@gmail.com>' is in AUTHORS on master.

This check now asserts the positive - that the entry is present - as well as the original facts. It asserted only the negative until the credit landed, and would have gone on reporting 'not yet credited' about a claim that had become an understatement.
metrics: co-author credit promised, not yet landed

claims.claim: Five open memory-safety issues in google/s2geometry, each with a standalone reproducer
claims.detail: NULL dereference on the library's documented traversal path (#674), out-of-bounds access from an unchecked shape id (#676), a 16 GiB allocation from unchecked counts (#677), a heap-buffer-overflow in EncodedS2LaxPolygonShape::edge (#678), and a 2.4 GiB allocation reachable from a 28-byte input (#679). The maintainer responded that these are not reachable as a denial of service because the decoder is assumed to run on trusted data, that the assumptions should be documented better, and that fixes for some were already in progress internally.

claims.claim: Two hardening pull requests under review in google/s2geometry, split at the maintainer's request
claims.detail: #681 validates loop_starts when decoding a lax polygon shape; #682 bounds untrusted counts in S2ShapeIndexCell::Decode. A third change (returning an empty cell instead of nullptr) was withdrawn after AddressSanitizer showed the crash it claimed to fix was the loop_starts out-of-bounds read.

claims.detail: The repository ships the 600-scenario corpus, the raw model outputs for every condition, and the analysis, plus its own checker (src/verify_reproducibility.py, run by `make verify`). claims.claim: tool-boundary-corpus - a labelled corpus of agent tool-boundary cases and a detector-agnostic harness that scores precision and recall
claims.detail: 23 cases (14 tool-list declarations, 5 framework-code, 4 declaration-drift) with positives citing where each pattern came from in the real world and negatives that are the correct implementation of the same job. Detectors are commands that print JSON, so any scanner can be scored. A drift case carries two states of the same server, because a declaration edited after approval -- the rug-pull shape -- cannot be expressed as one payload. Measured: mcpaudit P=1.000 R=1.000 on tool-list and on drift; agentbound P=1.000 R=1.000 on code, up from 0.750 when the corpus found a false positive it reported (a pattern inside a string bound to a name) -- agentbound v0.1.10 fixed it and the same harness re-measured the improvement. The harness is itself tested with fake detectors (perfect, silent, trigger-happy, crashing, malformed JSON), and the corpus is self-authored, which every report states.
metrics: found a real false positive that was then fixed

claims.claim: mcpaudit - review an MCP server's tool declarations before connecting, and pin them so a later change is visible
claims.detail: Static audit of a tools/list payload: reserved-name collisions (critical), instruction-shaped text, invisible Unicode with the tag-block payload decoded, look-alike tool names, destructive tools declaring readOnlyHint, unconstrained sink parameters. Silent on a well-behaved server, which is a test. A lock file with per-field hashes reports drift, including a changed description. It can also emit a starting policygate policy from the same declarations (deny/escalate/allow mapped from severity), which the integration tests load with the real policygate loader in CI. Writing the generator exposed a supply-chain bug in it: the tool name is attacker-controlled text written into the policy, and unescaped it could inject its own allow rule; every interpolated value is escaped now, with four regression tests.

claims.claim: policygate - a fail-closed policy gate for agent tool calls, built so a language model can never authorise an action
claims.detail: Rules are evaluated by severity rather than file order; ALLOW is produced only by an allow rule; a model may deny or escalate but its ALLOW on an uncovered call is overruled and recorded; a failing or unparseable evaluator falls through to the refusing default; every decision goes to a hash-chained audit log. Adapters wrap MCP-style servers, LangChain-style tools and provider-shaped function calls, duck-typed so no framework becomes a dependency. Verified by mutation: disabling the model-allow invariant fails three tests, disabling the unparseable-call path fails three, and disabling both fails six.

claims.claim: agentbound - static detector for AI-agent tool-boundary bugs
claims.detail: Nine detectors registered across Python, TypeScript and YAML for tool shadowing, reserved-name collisions, last-wins tool dictionaries, fail-open confirmation gates, and three rules covering AI agents dispatched on untrusted CI triggers; each grounded in a real finding. The README documents eight rows because the Go and Java variants share one. v0.1.11 is the current release and fixes a release that reported the wrong version: v0.1.10 shipped with `__version__` still at 0.1.9, so the tag, the release name and `agentbound --version` disagreed, and a test now compares the two version strings. The false positive that v0.1.10 fixed was found by sushant-me/tool-boundary-corpus: a string bound to a name is prose, not code.

claims.claim: Four published GitHub security advisories for vulnerabilities found and fixed in my own security tooling
claims.detail: GHSA-qwvv-fcmm-r3j2 (policygate, high) - a glob rule in the policy gate could be stepped around with a newline in the matched value, so a targeted deny rule was silently skipped and the call fell through to a broader allow. GHSA-wcqw-86xv-w95q (mcp-nameguard, medium) - unbounded reads let a hostile MCP server kill the scanner that was inspecting it. GHSA-mffv-hhg5-mm33 (agentbound, medium) - the masker blanked one-line assigned strings, hiding findings the scanner exists to report. GHSA-62f4-h552-54wc (mcpaudit, medium) - invisible-character ranges omitted the variation selector supplement and other channels, and the omission also survived the strip_invisible helper that is meant to show what text really contains. Each has a reproduction and a regression test; CVE identifiers requested from GitHub's CNA.

claims.claim: Merged a feature into a third-party bug-bounty engine that made 22 unreachable hunt-* skills routable
claims.detail: Auditing Claude-BugHunter's autonomy engine found 22 of its 58 hunt-* skills had no entry in CLASS_SKILL or TECH_SKILL, so they could never be selected and the routing loop silently degraded to hunt-misc. Completed the class (26 to 47), tech (10 to 20) and probe mappings; extended recon.py's deterministic classifier so those classes are actually emitted (websocket, cicd, k8s, cloud-misconfig, forgot-password, captcha-bypass, jwt-crypto, shadow-api, ato, mfa); covered every routed class in CLASS_WEIGHT so they rank by impact instead of the default; and added a coverage check that reports any installed hunt-* skill unreachable through a mapping. Self-tests and the repository's own linters pass. Credited as a contributor to the repository.
